statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-6766 is an integer underflow in NSS's tls13_AEAD(): when a TLS 1.3 record's ciphertext is shorter than the AEAD tag, subtracting the tag length from the input length wraps. Mozilla fixed it in Firefox 150 and Firefox ESR 140.10: https://www.mozilla.org/en-US/security/advisories/mfsa2026-30/#CVE-2026-6766. The fix, Mozilla bug 2023207, makes tls13_AEAD() in lib/ssl/tls13con.c fail with SEC_ERROR_INPUT_LEN before the subtraction when the input is shorter than the tag: https://hg-edge.mozilla.org/projects/nss/rev/42da9a7f8a03. The NSS 3.131.1, 3.132 and 3.134 release tags contain it. Debian fixed it in trixie in 2:3.110-1+deb13u2, DSA-6290-1, and lists 2:3.123-1 as the fixed version in unstable: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-6766. The DHI Debian repository publishes four builds of nss for Debian 13: a rebuild of Debian's 2:3.110-1+deb13u4 and builds of NSS 3.131.1, 3.132 and 3.134. We checked the libnss3 and libnss3-dbgsym packages of each on amd64 and arm64, verified against the index checksums: in every one, the disassembled tls13_AEAD() in libssl3.so has an error path that sets SEC_ERROR_INPUT_LEN (0xffffe004), an error code tls13_AEAD() in the NSS 3.110 release source does not use, next to the SEC_ERROR_INVALID_ARGS and SEC_ERROR_OUTPUT_LEN paths that both versions have. The libnssutil3.so version strings confirm NSS 3.110, 3.131.1, 3.132 and 3.134. As a control, tls13_AEAD() in Debian's unfixed libnss3 2:3.110-1+deb13u1 for amd64, matched to its debug symbols by build ID, has no SEC_ERROR_INPUT_LEN path. The changelog shipped in the 2:3.110-1+deb13u4 rebuild lists this CVE under Debian's 2:3.110-1+deb13u2 entry. Every published build carries the fix, so the range closes at the lowest published build, the 2:3.110-1+deb13u4 rebuild.
